findings.reason: the clause counts 256 construction-identical realisations as half the evidence for honesty, so a node and a reader treat a self-consistency identity as validation; dropping the arm, or restating it as a check that the receipt's covariance is the operator's inverse with the honesty claim rested on the 32 full fits alone (whose joint 99 % band over six directions is 0.386 to 1.99, the only falsifiable measure in the clause), changes what the node must produce and what the record may claim.
findings.text: clause (1)'s linearised arm propagates each noise realisation through "the fit's linearised least-squares operator" and divides the resulting variance by the receipt covariance, but that covariance is the same operator's Gram inverse, so the ratio is identically one whatever the covariance claims; measured on an arbitrary 40x2 response with propagation at the stated per-row scale, the empirical variance along the covariance's principal directions was 1.0036 and 1.0045 at 20,000 draws — the arm can only reveal that two implementations disagree, not whether the reported uncertainty is honest, and it is reported as one of the two arms that answer the section's question

response_events.note: The clause now rests the honesty test on the 32 full nonlinear fits alone, with their own interval, and restates the 256 linearised realisations as a check that the receipt covariance is the operator inverse, not as evidence of honesty.
